---
title: "Pareto-based hyperparameter tuning"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Pareto-based hyperparameter tuning}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Tuning holds graphs, factor dimensions and preprocessing fixed. Each candidate
has reconstruction loss R and **unweighted** roughness P, the sum of shared and
local graph trace penalties before multiplying by smoothing parameters. Weighted
penalties are unsuitable as the second objective because lambdas vary.

Both objectives are min-max normalized over eligible candidates. A constant
range maps to zero. The selected candidate minimizes
$\sqrt{\widetilde R^2+\widetilde P^2}$. Strictly nondominated candidates are also
reported. Exact distance ties select the first candidate in `expand.grid`
order (shared lambda changes fastest). The normalization, and therefore the
selected point, depends on the candidate grid.

```{r}
library(MSGPCA)
s <- simulation_gg_blocks(nside=6,Jsp=8,Jmix=12,Jns=10,seed=101)
f <- MSGPCA(lapply(s$Y_list,log1p),s$locs_list,n_shared=3,n_local=1,
             lambda_shared=c(.1,.3,.6),lambda_local=c(.1,.3),
             tuning='pareto',seed=101,verbose=FALSE)
f$optimal_lambda_shared
f$optimal_lambda_local
f$pareto_results
plot_pareto(f)
```

Use `lambda_constraint='shared_ge_local'` to require shared smoothing at least
local smoothing when both components are active; default imposes no restriction.
Disabled-component grids collapse to zero to avoid redundant fits.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Full empirical grid (kept out of routine vignette checks).
f <- tune_MSGPCA(lapply(s$Y_list,log1p),s$locs_list,
                 lambda_shared=seq(.1,.6,.1),lambda_local=seq(.1,.6,.1),
                 n_shared=3,n_local=1,lambda_constraint='shared_ge_local',
                 seed=101,verbose=FALSE)
```

Graphs are reused across candidates. Sparse factors are reused within each fit,
including identical shared/local systems, but released between candidates to
bound memory. Seeded initialization is consistent; no warm starts are used.
Only scalar candidate diagnostics are retained; the winning model is refitted.

Failed/nonfinite fits are excluded. Finite converged fits have priority. With
`nonconverged='fallback'` (default), finite nonconverged fits are eligible only
if no converged fit exists, with a warning. `nonconverged='exclude'` prohibits
that fallback. No eligible candidate is an error. The table retains failure
messages, iterations, timings, complete objective, convergence status, both
roughness terms, normalized criteria, front membership and selection flag.
NMI, ARI and truth labels are never used for tuning.
